open_blocking.title: False deadlock-freedom claim: the worker's trusted-hash RPC locks job_files before parts, the reverse of the new helper's parts-then-files order, and a 40P01 is reproducible at the head
open_blocking.evidence:
New helper order, in supabase/migrations/20261004100000_ovd598_serialize_legacy_xometry_admission.sql: parts FOR SHARE at :37, requirements at :38-42, then job_files FOR SHARE at :43-51. The helper is called at :110, before validation.

The reverse order is in public.api_register_trusted_file_hash (20261002... no: 20260812042000_add_canonical_part_identity.sql:316-380, its latest definition, granted to service_role at :383-384). It runs `select file.* ... for update` on the job_files row (:337-340), runs `update public.job_files ...` (:349), which also covers same-blob rows of other jobs in the org, and then loops over every part that references those files (:370-377), calling private.assign_canonical_part_version (:376). That function takes `select part.* ... for update` (:189-193). The worker calls this RPC on every staged storage download (worker/src/files.ts:41).

Reproduction at 9c18f46, local, after `supabase db reset --local`, under /tmp/ovd-supabase.lock. A driver held the requirement row FOR UPDATE only to park the request between its parts lock and its file lock; the driver is not part of the cycle. At t+2.7s, pg_stat_activity showed the request (pid 330) as a Lock waiter with blocked_by {329, the driver}, and the worker's real api_register_trusted_file_hash (pid 331) as a Lock waiter with blocked_by {330}, waiting on the part FOR UPDATE. After the driver committed, the request failed with: `REQUEST error sqlstate=40P01 msg=deadlock detected after_ms=4290 ctx=while locking tuple (0,1) in relation "job_files" | ... private.lock_xometry_beta_dispatch_scope_rows(uuid) line 10 at PERFORM`. The worker returned `WORKER ok after 3306 ms`.

Same interleaving against the pre-PR definition (20261002182910:343-520 re-applied, helper dropped): no Lock waiters, the worker finished in 8 ms, and the request failed only on eligibility, with no 40P01. So this PR introduces the cycle on the legacy path. The generic path has had the same order since 20261003160000:409-424.

In production the window covers any time the request is parked on a requirement row held by an editor, which is the R1 shape, and also concurrent staging of a same-blob file in another job of the same organization.

The result fails closed: the request rolls back and no permit is created. But the PR body's Rollback/risk notes say "A deadlock would need ... or an editor that takes the rows in an inverted order. Neither was found". The recorded row-order inversion check lists only api_update_client_part_request, api_reuse_trusted_part_version_artifacts, the reconciler, the delete fence and the enrollment RPC. The OVD-598 Linear rolling comment repeats R3's no-40P01 result as the deadlock evidence. The issue's deadlock watch (step 7) requires a 40P01 to be reported, not claimed absent.

There is a second, internal-only path with the same reversed order: a DELETE on job_files via RLS policy job_files_delete_internal cascades parts_cad_file_id_fkey ON DELETE SET NULL into parts rows, so it locks the file row and then the part rows.
open_blocking.suggested_fix:
1. Correct the PR body: the Rollback/risk notes and the round-1 row-order inversion paragraph under Review findings.
2. Correct the OVD-598 Linear rolling comment the same way. Record the reproduced inversion: worker trusted-hash staging, plus the internal job_files DELETE with SET NULL. Say that it fails closed with a 40P01 on one side, that the generic path shares it, and that R3 does not cover it.
3. Do not change the admission lock order or lock strength without review (issue step 7).
4. Then either open a bounded follow-up or child issue to make api_register_trusted_file_hash lock the referencing parts (ordered by id) before it updates job_files, with a dblink race for it, or record an explicit reviewer/owner disposition accepting the residual for this release.
